avalancheActivity.comment: The main concern is wind-drifted snow on the leeward sides (W, SE, and S) of the highest elevations. Be cautious in very steep areas, narrow gullies, slopes below rock faces, and terrain depressions where snow accumulates in large quantities and forms snow cushions, slabs, and drifts. Prolonged low temperatures and a thin snowpack lead to the development of critical—permanently weak—layers within the snowpack. Avalanches may be triggered primarily by significant additional loading, though the occurrence of smaller spontaneous avalanches from slab snow cannot be ruled out.
avalancheActivity.highlights: In the highest elevations of the High, Western, and Low Tatras (above 1,700 m a.s.l.), the avalanche danger remains MODERATE—Level 2.

snowpackStructure.comment: Cold air of Arctic origin continues to linger over Slovakia, bringing snowfall from the north accompanied by strong NW to S winds. Over the past 2–3 days, 10 to 30 cm of new snow has fallen; a continuous snowpack is already present from the foothills onward, with significant depths found above the tree line, where it reaches 30 to 70 cm, and locally even more. Partly due to low temperatures, the snow layers are not sufficiently bonded together. Due to the wind, the snow cover is distributed unevenly.

avalancheActivity.comment: In the highest elevations of the mountain range, fresh snow has been blown by the wind onto leeward (E, SE, S) slopes, into gullies and hollows, where unstable snow slabs, pillows, and drifts have formed. Under additional loading, small avalanches consisting of snow slabs may be triggered on steep slopes.
avalancheActivity.highlights: In the Fatra Mountains and the eastern part of the Low Tatras, a LOW avalanche danger (Level 1) has developed above the tree line.

snowpackStructure.comment: Between 5 and 25 cm of fresh snow has fallen in the mountains, but due to wind, it is distributed very unevenly. On leeward (E, SE, S) slopes, there are locally up to 50 cm of wind-blown, unstable snow. Due to low temperatures, the snowpack will stabilize only slowly.
